## What makes it different

Every single pixel and every single sound in this game is **generated by code at runtime**.
There are no `.png`, `.jpg`, `.mp3` or `.wav` files anywhere in this repository.

| | How it's done |
|---|---|
| **Art** | Canvas 2D paths, gradients and seeded noise. Rocks and nuggets are irregular blobs from a seeded RNG, so no two are alike. The cave background is pre-rendered once to an offscreen canvas. |
| **Sound** | Web Audio oscillators, biquad filters and generated noise buffers. |
| **Music** | A 16th-note step sequencer with a lookahead scheduler, playing a 4-bar Am–Am–F–G loop. |
| **Randomness** | A `mulberry32` PRNG seeded per level, so a given level always looks identical. |

The whole thing is ~2,700 lines of dependency-free ES5-compatible JavaScript.

## Features

- **20 hand-tuned levels** plus an **endless mode** after you clear them
- **3 difficulties** (Casual / Classic / Hardcore) with independent high-score saves
- **13 item types** — nuggets in 4 sizes, diamonds, mystery bags, treasure chests, rocks, gem-bearing rocks, bones, skulls, TNT barrels and burrowing moles
- **Weight-based physics** — a huge nugget crawls back up, a diamond snaps back instantly
- **Combo system** — chain valuable hauls for up to a ×1.5 multiplier
- **7-item shop** between levels: dynamite, strength books, diamond polish, lucky clover, rock collector's book, pocket watch, energy drink
- **Gem-bearing rocks** that are nearly worthless if you haul them, but drop a diamond if you blow them up
- **S / A / B / C grading** at the end of every level
- **Procedural background music** you can toggle independently from SFX
- Full **keyboard, mouse and touch** support, plus a responsive layout for phones
- High scores persisted in `localStorage`

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Mouse / Touch |
|---|---|---|
| Drop the claw | <kbd>Space</kbd> / <kbd>↓</kbd> | Click or tap the stage |
| Detonate dynamite | <kbd>D</kbd> | The **引爆** button (bottom left) |
| Pause | <kbd>P</kbd> / <kbd>Esc</kbd> | The pause button |
| Toggle SFX | <kbd>M</kbd> | The SFX button |
| Toggle music | <kbd>N</kbd> | The music button |
| Confirm dialogs | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Click the primary button |

## Play it

**Online** — <https://lor3walker.github.io/gold-miner/>

**One file, offline** — download [`dist/gold-miner.html`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lor3walker/gold-miner/main/dist/gold-miner.html) (right-click the link, *Save link as…*) and double-click it. 99 KB, no server, no install, runs straight from `file://`.

**From source**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Lor3walker/gold-miner.git
cd gold-miner
open index.html          # or just double-click it
```

Optionally serve it over HTTP (nothing here requires it, but it's closer to production):

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8765
# → http://localhost:8765
```

## Build the single-file bundle

`build.js` inlines the stylesheet and all nine scripts into one self-contained HTML file. It uses only Node's standard library — there is nothing to install.

```bash
node build.js
# → dist/gold-miner.html  (99 KB)
```

It escapes any `</script` sequences in the inlined code and aborts if it finds an external reference it could not inline, so a broken bundle never ships.

## Project structure

```
index.html              markup + canvas + HUD buttons
css/style.css           layout, modals, responsive rules
js/
  utils.js       116     RNG, math, blob paths, localStorage helpers
  audio.js       258     Web Audio SFX + music sequencer
  sprites.js     877     every drawing routine (miner, cave, items, rope)
  items.js        71     item table: value, weight, radius, depth bias
  level.js       137     goals, difficulty curves, spawn placement
  hook.js        178     pendulum swing, extend/retract state machine
  game.js        717     game loop, scoring, shop, HUD, level flow
  ui.js          234     DOM modals (menu, shop, results) + wiring
  main.js        108     bootstrap, input handling, requestAnimationFrame
build.js                single-file bundler
.github/workflows/      GitHub Pages deployment
```

Modules attach themselves to a single `window.GM` namespace and load as classic
`<script>` tags rather than ES modules — that is deliberate, and it's the reason
the game runs when opened directly from the filesystem.

## Implementation notes

<details>
<summary><strong>Swing and hook physics</strong></summary>

The claw is a pendulum pivoting at the miner's winch, sweeping ±76°. While
extending, the rope advances in sub-steps of at most 12 px and tests for
collisions at each step, so a fast claw can never tunnel through a small nugget.

Retract speed is `900 × strength / weight`, clamped to 48–620 px/s. That single
line produces the whole risk/reward feel of the original: a 500-point nugget
weighs 12 and takes forever, a 600-point diamond weighs 1.6 and comes home
almost instantly.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Guaranteed-reachable spawns</strong></summary>

Items are placed with rejection sampling — up to 260 attempts each, honouring a
per-item depth preference and a no-overlap rule. Crucially, every candidate
position is validated against the claw's actual reach: at depth `dy` the
horizontal half-range is `min(dy × tan(76°), √(760² − dy²))`. Shallow far
corners are therefore excluded automatically, and the game can never spawn
treasure you are physically unable to grab.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Procedural sprites</strong></summary>

Nuggets and rocks are built from `blobPath()` — a closed path of radius-jittered
vertices from the item's own seed — then clipped and filled with facet triangles
to fake crystalline shading. The cave wall is drawn once into an offscreen
canvas: gradient base, then timber supports, then hairline strata cracks, then
2,600 grain specks layered on top so the supports read as *buried in* the dirt
rather than sitting on it.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Music without audio files</strong></summary>

A `setInterval` scheduler runs every 40 ms and queues Web Audio events up to
200 ms ahead, which keeps timing sample-accurate without depending on the
render loop. Bass and lead voices step through fixed patterns transposed by the
current bar's root note. SFX and music sit on separate gain buses so they can be
muted independently.

</details>

## Browser support

Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari — desktop and mobile. Requires Canvas 2D and,
for sound, Web Audio (audio unlocks on your first interaction, as browsers
require). Under `file://` some browsers block `localStorage`; the code handles
that gracefully and simply won't persist high scores.

## A note on language

The in-game interface is in **Chinese** (the game is a tribute to a title that
was hugely popular in Chinese web-game arcades). The code, comments in this
README and the API are English. Everything is playable without reading a word —
the controls table above is all you need.
